Finite enumeration does not prove the asymptotics.

originality.rationale: The claimed object is the second-order probability of at least one common non-cherry proper clade in two independent rooted YHK trees, plus conditional localization at a triple. Published Poisson overlap of tree comparisons and exact single-tree clade marginals/joints are acknowledged as ingredients, not claimed as new. The second-order nested/disjoint decomposition does not follow from a first-order Poisson overlap law; potential historical coverage in 1993 paper remains a material residual risk.
residual_risks: The 1993 Steel–Penny complete article could not be read: its abstract's broad Poisson tree-comparison statement may conceal an overlap result closer than presently verified.

The published one-tree clade probability calculus can imply many two-tree identities; this work claims only the explicit second-order probability and structural cancellation, not those underlying formulas.
The value is a sharp natural rare-event refinement, not a general theorem for other tree models.

value.rationale: The exact first two coefficients quantify the first non-cherry agreement of two independent rooted speciation histories. It is a natural size-restricted Robinson–Foulds null event and distinguishes triple, quadruple, nested and disjoint mechanisms; conditional localization makes the event interpretable. It is not a gratuitous finite-parameter recomputation.
